beats.text: Thirty three million dollars got spent to stop one man from winning one election
and he still won it by less than one point.
So what would happen if Abdul El-Sayed became the president of the United States?
Look at that crowd. When this man walks into a room people scream his name and when I walk into a room the dog leaves.
I want to be like him so badly that I bought a suit and the suit asked for a refund.
Stick around because by the end of this you will know exactly who would fight the hardest to stop him.
He is a doctor whose dad came from Egypt and right now he is running for the Senate in Michigan but today we are making him president.
And he really could because he was born in Michigan and the Constitution only asks that you are born an American and at least thirty five.
Remember those thirty three million dollars? A super PAC linked to AIPAC spent it in his Senate primary to help somebody else.
It did not work.
Then there is the current president who keeps calling him Mohammed on Truth Social and wrote that he goes back to the days of the Jihad.
And El-Sayed answered that Trump knows his name is Abdul because he says it every day.
His opponent even claimed he pledged support to the Muslim Brotherhood but a fact check found no evidence at all.
So what would really change for you and who would fight the hardest to stop him?
So it is day one and President El-Sayed walks into the office and the first thing on the desk is the plan he talks about the most which is Medicare for All.
The idea is simple to say and very hard to do because the government becomes everybody's basic health insurance and the doctor bill goes to Washington instead of to you.
His campaign says you could still keep extra insurance from your job or your union but it should become redundant and unnecessary.
Now the price. When Bernie Sanders had a plan like this in 2020 the Urban Institute said it would cost the federal government thirty four trillion dollars over ten years.
And a fellow at that same institute told reporters this year that with inflation it could now cost close to double that.
Sixty something trillion. I checked my wallet. Not enough.

So who pays? Here it gets honest because El-Sayed has said he would try to make the rich pay and that he hopes to avoid raising taxes on most families including people who earn around a hundred thousand dollars a year.

But his campaign did not say exactly how it would pay for it and a budget watchdog group called the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget said back in 2019 that taxes on the middle class would have to rise to pay for Medicare for All.
That same group also said that a lot of families could end up paying less in taxes than they pay today in premiums and copays.
So your paycheck might lose a piece on one side and win a bigger piece on the other side and nobody can tell you which one until the plan has real numbers.
Bridge Michigan checked it and their bottom line was that the claim it would raise taxes is likely correct but some experts think the total cost could go down for some families.
So day one ends with one plan and zero laws. Hold that thought.
In week one he goes after something every renter in America feels which is the rent.
He has vowed to ban large corporations from owning homes at all and to ban the computer programs that big landlords use to set rents together.
He also wants companies like Airbnb to pay a special fee for pushing people out of their neighborhoods.
The picture in your head is a big company buying up the whole street but a housing expert at Michigan State said corporate buyers are only about two percent of the single family market.
Two percent. That is one house on a street of fifty. Rude house though.

And here is the funny part because a ban on big investors buying houses is not even only his idea. This year Congress passed a bipartisan housing bill that stops investors who already own three hundred and fifty homes from buying more.
So on this one he might find friends on both sides which in Washington is rarer than a cheap apartment.
But week one was the easy part because in month one the people with the most money start writing checks.
Remember those thirty three million dollars from the start? Cute.
By the beginning of October the money spent in his Senate race had passed two hundred and five million dollars and it was on pace to become the most expensive election Michigan has ever seen.
Republican groups alone had spent fifty nine million dollars on that race.
And there were another sixty five million dollars of ads already booked until Election Day and about forty two million of that was there to help Rogers.
And that same AIPAC super PAC from the primary is now reported to be sending up to nine million dollars to a group that backs his Republican opponent Mike Rogers.
Have a guess how much the groups backing him had spent. Twenty three million.

He does get help from big names though because Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez sent a million dollars to help his side. And keep an eye on Fox News because later in this video one of their hosts says something about him that nobody saw coming.
But the biggest wall is not money it is math. A president cannot pass a law alone. In the Senate a bill needs a majority and most big bills need sixty votes to get past a filibuster.
So President El-Sayed would need sixty senators to say yes to Medicare for All and getting sixty senators to agree on something this big is about the hardest thing you can do in Washington.
Laws passed in month one. Still zero.
And that is when it stops being about his plans and starts being about him.
And then there is everything that gets thrown at him personally.
You already heard about the Mohammed nickname and the Muslim Brotherhood claim that a fact check found no evidence for.

Then on October twenty fifth the current president held a rally in Port Huron Michigan and told the crowd and I am quoting him exactly I'm here to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator.
El-Sayed has said again and again that he is loyal to the United States and he has disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood.
And when Mike Rogers questioned his loyalty in a debate El-Sayed called it shameful and said I'm proud of our Constitution that guarantees all of us the right to pray as we choose to pray.
And before that rally he even taunted the president and said Donald if you're watching don't wuss out man.
That is a real quote.
Even the interviews get rough because he once said that being interviewed on CNN felt like and I am quoting him again I get a non-consensual colonoscopy.
He is a doctor so he would know.
He is also attacked for what he says about Gaza. He has said Israel's government committed genocide in Gaza and that he opposes unconditional military aid to Israel.
His critics call those positions extreme and his supporters call them honest and you will hear both every single day of this presidency.
So picture month two. The money is against him and the math is against him and half the news is against him.
But before you decide what he could do as president there is one job he already did and it is the best test we have.
And then something weird happens because after a long and heated interview on Fox News the host Jesse Watters said he actually likes him.
Even Fox.

So can this guy run anything? We actually have a test. In 2015 Detroit had just come out of bankruptcy and its health department had been handed to private companies and the mayor gave it to a thirty year old doctor to rebuild.
In his first year the department more than doubled in size.
After the Flint water crisis his team tested the water in every Detroit public school building which was ninety four buildings and they found nineteen schools with too much lead or copper.
Ninety four buildings. I cannot even test my fridge.

Now to be fair his campaign said he removed the lead from those schools and a news site found that the fixes were temporary and later tests still found lead so the honest version is that his team found the problem.
His department also gave more than five thousand pairs of free glasses to kids in Detroit schools.
Before all that he was a Rhodes Scholar and he got his medical degree at Columbia.
And remember those books from the very start? They are real. He wrote one called Healing Politics and a whole guide to Medicare for All with another doctor called Micah Johnson.
He even hosts a podcast called America Dissected.
Two books and a podcast. I have a library card. It expired.
Then in 2017 he left to run for governor of Michigan and in 2018 he lost that primary to Gretchen Whitmer.
So now you have the plans and the walls and the record which means we can finally answer the question from the very start.
So here is the deal.
If President El-Sayed got his way your health insurance would come from the government and your taxes and premiums would both change and big companies could not buy your street.

So who would fight the hardest to stop him? Not one single person. It is the hundreds of millions of dollars and the sixty votes he would need in the Senate and a country where half the people would fight every one of those plans.
So would he change everything? Absolutely ... nothing in the first month. But that is true for every president because a president is a pen and Congress is the paper.

And remember he is not even a senator yet. Republicans have not won a Senate race in Michigan for more than three decades but this year they see an opening and he is up against Mike Rogers who is a former congressman backed by the current president.
If El-Sayed wins he would be the first Muslim senator.
And it all starts on November third when Michigan decides if he even gets to the Senate.
Which one of his plans would you keep and which one would you throw out? Tell me in the comments.
Money talks so make sure yours says something smart. See you next time.
